passage.title: The Impact of Wildfires on Natural Landscapes
passage.text:
Wildfires are one of the most powerful natural forces on Earth, capable of transforming vast areas of land within hours. Every year, millions of hectares of forests, grasslands, and shrublands burn across the globe, from the dry hills of California to the dense forests of Australia and the open savannas of Africa. While many people think of wildfires only as disasters that destroy everything in their path, scientists and ecologists have come to understand that fire plays a far more complex role in the natural world. In many ecosystems, fire is not simply a destructive event — it is an essential part of how the land renews and sustains itself over time.

One of the most visible effects of a wildfire is the immediate damage it causes to vegetation. Trees, shrubs, and grasses are burned away, and the landscape can look completely lifeless in the days and weeks after a fire passes through. However, this appearance is often misleading. Many plants in fire-prone regions have developed remarkable ways of surviving and recovering from flames. Some trees, such as certain species of eucalyptus and pine, produce seeds that are only released when exposed to the intense heat of a fire. Others have thick bark that insulates them from the worst of the heat, allowing the living tissue inside the trunk to survive even when the outer surface is badly charred. These natural adaptations mean that a landscape that looks devastated immediately after a fire may begin showing new green growth within just a few weeks.

The effect of wildfires on soil is another important aspect that is often overlooked. When plant material burns, it releases nutrients that had been stored in leaves, branches, and roots directly into the soil in the form of ash. This sudden influx of nutrients — particularly nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium — can significantly enrich the soil and support the rapid growth of new vegetation. At the same time, however, intense fires can also damage the top layer of soil, reducing its ability to absorb water and making it more vulnerable to erosion by wind and rain. The overall impact on soil health depends greatly on how hot the fire burns and how long it lasts, with low-intensity fires generally being more beneficial and high-intensity fires more likely to cause lasting harm.

Wildlife is also deeply affected by wildfires, though not always in the ways that people expect. In the short term, animals that cannot escape a fast-moving fire may be killed, and those that survive often lose the food sources and shelters they depend on. But in the weeks and months that follow, recovering landscapes frequently attract a surprising variety of animal life. The fresh new plant growth that emerges after a fire is often more nutritious and easier to eat than older vegetation, drawing grazing animals such as deer and elk in large numbers. Birds that feed on insects are also commonly seen in recently burned areas, where the exposed ground makes it easier to find prey. Some species, including certain types of woodpeckers, actually prefer recently burned forests because the dead trees provide ideal nesting sites and a rich supply of wood-boring insects.

Not all wildfires, however, are part of a natural cycle. In many parts of the world, the size, frequency, and intensity of fires have increased dramatically in recent decades due to a combination of human activity and climate change. Extended periods of drought, rising temperatures, and the accumulation of large amounts of dry plant material — partly a result of decades of fire suppression policies — have created conditions in which fires burn hotter and spread farther than they did historically. In these situations, the damage caused by fires can exceed what natural ecosystems are able to recover from, permanently altering the character of the landscape and threatening species that have not evolved to cope with fire at such extreme levels.

Understanding the difference between natural fire and human-influenced fire has become one of the central challenges facing land managers and conservationists around the world. In response, many countries have adopted a practice known as "prescribed burning" — the deliberate, controlled use of fire to reduce the buildup of dry vegetation before it can fuel a larger, uncontrolled blaze. By mimicking the low-intensity fires that once occurred naturally in many ecosystems, prescribed burning helps restore balance to fire-adapted landscapes and reduces the risk of catastrophic wildfires. When used carefully and with proper planning, this approach represents one of the most effective tools available for protecting both natural environments and the communities that live near them.

tasks.suggestion:
Để đạt kết quả tốt cho phần thi này, bạn nên áp dụng các chiến thuật sau đây:

  • Dạng câu hỏi Ý chính (R1Q1): Sử dụng kỹ năng Skimming (Đọc lướt). Đọc lướt đoạn đầu và đoạn cuối để nắm trọn vẹn luận điểm chính. Bài viết không đơn thuần nói về thiệt hại, biến đổi khí hậu hay chỉ gói gọn ở sự thích nghi của sinh vật. Luận điểm bao quát là dù cháy rừng thường bị coi là thảm họa thuần túy, chúng đóng một vai trò sinh thái phức tạp và đòi hỏi các biện pháp quản lý cẩn trọng để cân bằng giữa lợi ích và rủi ro.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Chi tiết (R1Q2, R1Q4, R1Q6, R1Q8, R1Q9): Sử dụng kỹ năng Scanning (Đọc quét) từ khóa để khoanh vùng thông tin gốc. Với R1Q2, quét đoạn 2 tìm từ khóa "eucalyptus" và "pine" để thấy đặc điểm: hạt giống của chúng chỉ được giải phóng khi nhiệt độ cực cao của đám cháy kích hoạt sự mở ra của quả/nón, cho phép chúng phát triển sau khi lửa tắt. Với R1Q4, quét đoạn 3 tìm từ khóa "soil" và "nutrients" để thấy tác động: việc đốt cháy vật liệu thực vật giải phóng các chất dinh dưỡng dự trữ vào đất dưới dạng tro, giúp hỗ trợ sự tái sinh nhanh chóng của cây non. Với R1Q6, quét đoạn 4 tìm từ khóa "woodpecker" để làm rõ lý do: rừng sau cháy cung cấp các cây chết lý tưởng để làm tổ và chứa quần thể lớn côn trùng đục gỗ làm thức ăn cho chúng. Với R1Q8, quét đoạn 5 và 6 để tìm tổ hợp các nguyên nhân: hạn hán kéo dài, nhiệt độ cao hơn và sự tích tụ của thảm thực vật khô do hệ quả của hàng thập kỷ dập tắt các đám cháy tự nhiên. Với R1Q9, tìm phần thảo luận về tác động của lửa lên đất để thấy yếu tố quyết định: chính là nhiệt độ và thời gian kéo dài của đám cháy, lửa cường độ thấp làm giàu đất còn lửa cường độ cao dễ gây ra thiệt hại lâu dài.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Từ vựng & Quy chiếu (R1Q3, R1Q5): Phân tích dựa trên ngữ cảnh trực tiếp. Với R1Q3, đại từ "them" nằm trong vế "insulates them from the worst of the heat". Đối chiếu ngược lại câu trước, lớp vỏ dày ("thick bark") bao bọc và bảo vệ cho chính các cây cối ("trees") đó. Với R1Q5, cụm từ "prescribed burning" được định nghĩa rõ ràng ngay trong đoạn 6 là việc sử dụng lửa có kế hoạch và được kiểm soát để loại bỏ thảm thực vật khô, giảm nguy cơ cháy rừng ngoài tầm kiểm soát.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Loại trừ NOT (R1Q7): Tiến hành đối soát danh sách động vật ở đoạn 4. Văn bản nhắc đến hươu và nai sừng tấm, các loài chim ăn côn trùng trên mặt đất mở, và chim gõ kiến. Loài sói tận dụng thảm thực vật giảm để săn mồi hoàn toàn không xuất hiện, do đó đây là đáp án cần chọn.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Suy luận (R1Q10): Đọc sâu phần cảnh báo ở đoạn 5. Khi các vụ cháy cường độ cao tăng tần suất, ta suy luận được rằng một số hệ sinh thái có thể bị thay đổi vĩnh viễn vượt quá khả năng phục hồi tự nhiên, đe dọa các loài vốn tiến hóa để thích nghi với điều kiện cháy cường độ thấp chứ không phải cực đoan.

Lời khuyên: Đây là bài đọc khoa học tự nhiên có cấu trúc thông tin rất rõ ràng. Hãy xử lý các câu Từ vựng (R1Q5) và Quy chiếu (R1Q3) trước để lấy đà. Tiếp theo, dùng từ khóa quét nhanh cho các câu Chi tiết (R1Q2, R1Q4, R1Q6, R1Q8, R1Q9) và câu NOT (R1Q7). Cuối cùng, tổng hợp mạch lập luận của tác giả để chốt chính xác đáp án cho câu Ý chính (R1Q1) và câu Suy luận (R1Q10).

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Wildfires cause serious damage to forests and grasslands, but prescribed burning offers a reliable method for preventing them from spreading to nearby communities.
Many plants and animals in fire-prone regions have developed remarkable adaptations that allow them to survive and recover quickly after a wildfire passes through.
Although wildfires are widely seen as purely destructive, they play a complex role in natural ecosystems and require careful management to balance their benefits and risks.
The increasing size and intensity of wildfires around the world is primarily the result of climate change, which has made traditional fire suppression methods ineffective.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is unusual about the seeds of certain eucalyptus and pine trees?
options: They are dispersed by wind immediately after a fire and can travel long distances to colonize areas outside the burned zone.
They contain nutrients absorbed from ash-enriched soil that give them a higher chance of survival than seeds from non-fire-adapted species.
They are only released from the tree when the extreme heat of a fire triggers their opening, allowing them to grow after the fire ends.
They are stored underground in protective casings that prevent them from being damaged by the heat of passing fires.

questions.question: The word "them" in paragraph 2 refers to _______.
options: the trees that have developed thick bark as protection against fire damage
the seeds that are released by eucalyptus and pine trees after a fire
the scientists and ecologists who study plant adaptations in burned landscapes
the flames that move through fire-prone regions during a wildfire

questions.question: According to the passage, how does burning plant material affect the soil?
options: It removes all harmful bacteria from the soil surface, creating a sterile environment that is ideal for the establishment of new plant species.
It increases the soil's ability to retain water by creating a layer of charred material that slows the movement of rain into deeper layers.
It permanently hardens the top layer of soil, making it difficult for new roots to penetrate the ground in the years after a fire.
It releases nutrients stored in vegetation into the soil as ash, which can support the rapid regrowth of new plants.

questions.question: The word "prescribed burning" in paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to _______.
options: a scientific technique for studying how different types of ecosystems respond to fire under controlled laboratory conditions
a planned and managed use of fire to remove dry vegetation and lower the risk of uncontrolled wildfires
a legal requirement for landowners in fire-prone areas to clear vegetation from around their properties each year
a natural fire cycle that occurs in forests at regular intervals without any human involvement

questions.question: According to the passage, why do some woodpecker species prefer recently burned forests?
options: The open canopy created by a fire allows more sunlight to reach the forest floor, which encourages the growth of berries and fruits that woodpeckers eat.
Burned forests provide dead trees that are ideal for nesting and that contain large populations of wood-boring insects for woodpeckers to feed on.
The absence of larger predators in burned areas gives woodpeckers a safer environment in which to raise their young during the recovery period.
The nutrient-rich ash deposited in burned forests attracts a greater variety of insect species than are typically found in unburned areas.

questions.question: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT mentioned as an animal that benefits from the conditions found in a landscape after a wildfire?
options: Wolves that use the reduced vegetation cover in burned areas to more easily track and hunt their prey
Birds that feed on insects exposed by the burned and open ground left behind after a fire
Deer and elk that are drawn to the more nutritious new plant growth that appears after a fire
Woodpeckers that use dead trees left by fires for nesting and as a source of wood-boring insects

questions.question: According to the passage, what combination of factors has caused wildfires to become more destructive in recent decades?
options: The decline of large grazing animals has allowed dry vegetation to accumulate in forests, while warmer ocean temperatures have reduced rainfall across fire-prone regions.
The expansion of farmland into forested areas has created new sources of ignition, while air pollution from industrial activity has made vegetation more flammable than in the past.
Longer droughts, higher temperatures, and the buildup of dry plant material linked partly to decades of suppressing natural fires have all contributed to more intense and widespread fires.
Invasive plant species introduced from other regions have replaced native fire-adapted vegetation with species that burn more easily and regenerate more slowly after a fire.

questions.question: According to the passage, what determines whether the effect of a wildfire on soil is mostly beneficial or mostly harmful?
options: The season in which the fire occurs, since fires in dry summer months tend to burn more completely and cause more soil damage than those in cooler seasons.
The slope of the land where the fire burns, since steep terrain increases the speed of erosion after a fire regardless of how hot or cool the fire itself was.
The temperature and duration of the fire, with lower-intensity fires being more likely to enrich the soil and high-intensity fires more likely to cause lasting damage.
The type of vegetation that was growing in the area before the fire, since different plant species release different quantities and combinations of nutrients when they burn.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the passage about what might happen to fire-adapted ecosystems if large, high-intensity wildfires continue to increase in frequency?
options: Wildlife populations in fire-prone areas will gradually decline as animals migrate permanently to regions where fire does not occur, leaving recovering landscapes without the grazers that aid regrowth.
Some ecosystems may be permanently changed beyond their natural capacity to recover, threatening species that evolved for lower-intensity fire conditions rather than extreme ones.
Governments will be forced to abandon prescribed burning programs because the increasing frequency of natural fires will make additional controlled burning too dangerous to carry out safely.
Plants that produce fire-triggered seeds will eventually become the dominant species in affected regions because they are the only ones capable of surviving repeated intense fires.

passage.title: The Evolution of International Education
passage.text:
The movement of students across national borders in pursuit of education is not a modern phenomenon. Scholars traveled from across the medieval Islamic world to study at institutions such as the House of Wisdom in Baghdad, and European universities in Bologna, Paris, and Oxford drew students from dozens of countries as early as the twelfth and thirteenth centuries. Yet the scale, structure, and motivations of what we now call international education have undergone a transformation so substantial in the past half-century that historical precedents offer only partial illumination of the contemporary landscape. Today, international student mobility is a multi-billion-dollar industry, a component of national foreign policy, a driver of university revenue, and — for the students themselves — a life decision shaped by an increasingly complex web of economic calculation, cultural aspiration, and professional strategy.

The postwar expansion of international education was driven initially by idealist impulses closely tied to the broader project of constructing multilateral institutions and fostering cross-cultural understanding. Programs such as the Fulbright Scholarship, established in the United States in 1946, were premised on the belief that educational exchange could reduce international tensions by creating personal and intellectual connections between citizens of different nations. Similar logic underpinned the proliferation of scholarship programs funded by national governments and international organizations throughout the 1950s and 1960s. During this period, the flow of students was predominantly from the developing world to established academic centers in North America and Western Europe, a pattern that reflected existing geopolitical hierarchies but was justified, at least rhetorically, through the language of development assistance and knowledge transfer.

By the 1980s and 1990s, the idealist framework had not disappeared but had been substantially overlaid by a commercial one. Universities in English-speaking countries — particularly the United Kingdom, Australia, the United States, and Canada — began to recognize international students as a significant source of tuition revenue at a time when public funding for higher education was declining. The active recruitment of fee-paying international students transformed admissions practices, gave rise to an entire industry of education agents and pathway programs, and introduced a market logic into decisions that had previously been governed primarily by academic criteria. For the receiving institutions, the financial benefits were considerable; for the students, the expanding availability of overseas study options created new opportunities but also new vulnerabilities, including exposure to institutions whose primary interest was revenue rather than educational quality.

The motivations of international students themselves have also evolved considerably over this period. Research conducted in the early 2000s consistently found that academic reputation was the primary factor driving destination choice, with students selecting institutions that offered programs unavailable or of lower quality in their home countries. By the 2010s, however, studies documented a measurable shift toward what researchers termed "migration-linked" motivations — the pursuit of overseas study as a pathway to permanent residency or labor market access in the destination country rather than as an end in itself. This shift was particularly pronounced among students from countries with limited domestic employment opportunities for graduates, and it introduced a new set of considerations into international education policy, as receiving countries began to grapple with the question of whether student visa systems were functioning as intended or had become de facto immigration pathways.

The geographical distribution of international student flows has also shifted markedly in recent decades. For most of the postwar period, the dominant pattern was one of flow from the global South to a small number of anglophone destinations. Since the 2000s, this pattern has become considerably more complex. The emergence of China, Singapore, and Malaysia as significant regional education hubs has created new circuits of student mobility within Asia that do not pass through traditional Western destinations. Meanwhile, several European countries have developed aggressive internationalization strategies, attracting students with low or no tuition fees and high-quality programs taught in English, while Gulf states have sought to establish branch campuses of prestigious foreign universities on their own soil. The result is a multipolar landscape in which the dominance of any single national higher education system is less assured than it appeared two decades ago.

Technology has introduced yet another dimension of complexity into the international education landscape. The rapid growth of online learning platforms and, more recently, the widespread adoption of hybrid and fully remote degree programs by established universities have decoupled some of the core assumptions underlying international student mobility — namely, that gaining access to high-quality education requires physical relocation to a different country. For students in lower-income countries who cannot afford the full costs of overseas study — tuition, living expenses, travel, and visa fees — online provision has opened access to programs that would otherwise be beyond reach. At the same time, the social, professional, and cultural dimensions of the overseas study experience — the networks built, the languages practiced, the environments navigated — remain difficult to replicate in a virtual setting, and demand for physical mobility has thus far proven more resilient than early predictions of online learning's disruption suggested.

What the evolution of international education ultimately reveals is that student mobility has never been a simple matter of individuals pursuing knowledge wherever it can be best obtained. It has always been shaped by the policies of states, the interests of institutions, the structures of global inequality, and the particular aspirations that different historical moments make available to different populations of students. Understanding international education in the twenty-first century requires holding all of these dimensions simultaneously in view — neither reducing it to a market transaction nor romanticizing it as a purely intellectual or humanistic enterprise, but recognizing it as a phenomenon in which idealism, commerce, policy, and individual ambition are inextricably entangled.

tasks.suggestion:
Để đạt kết quả tốt cho phần thi này, bạn nên áp dụng các chiến thuật sau đây:

  • Dạng câu hỏi Ý chính & Thái độ tác giả (R2Q1, R2Q10): Sử dụng kỹ năng Skimming (Đọc lướt). Đọc lướt đoạn đầu và đoạn cuối để nắm bắt mạch lập luận toàn cục. Với R2Q1, bài viết tránh các góc nhìn phiến diện chỉ quy về thương mại hóa hay công nghệ trực tuyến; luận điểm cốt lõi là sự dịch chuyển của sinh viên qua biên giới luôn được định hình bởi tổ hợp các yếu tố chính trị, thương mại và cá nhân, và việc hiểu hiện tượng này đòi hỏi phải nhìn nhận thấu đáo tất cả các chiều kích phức tạp đó. Với R2Q10, tác giả nhìn nhận công nghệ trực tuyến giúp mở rộng tiếp cận nhưng không thể thay thế hoàn toàn di động thể chất, vì các khía cạnh xã hội và mạng lưới chuyên nghiệp của việc du học trực tiếp rất khó tái tạo trong môi trường ảo.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Chi tiết (R2Q2, R2Q3, R2Q5, R2Q7, R2Q8): Sử dụng kỹ năng Scanning (Đọc quét) để định vị thông tin dựa trên từ khóa. Với R2Q2, quét đoạn 2 tìm từ khóa "Fulbright Scholarship" hoặc "1946" để thấy mục đích thành lập: giảm thiểu căng thẳng quốc tế bằng cách xây dựng các mối quan hệ cá nhân và trí tuệ giữa công dân các nước qua trao đổi giáo dục. Với R2Q3, quét đoạn 3 tìm mốc thời gian "1980s" và các nước nói tiếng Anh để thấy hệ quả: sự bùng nổ của ngành tuyển sinh thương mại đã đưa các ưu tiên định hướng thị trường vào quyết định tuyển sinh, vốn trước đây chủ yếu dựa trên học thuật. Với R2Q5, đối soát mốc thời gian "2000s" và "2010s" ở đoạn 4 để thấy sự chuyển dịch động lực: sinh viên dần dịch chuyển từ việc ưu tiên danh tiếng học thuật sang việc coi du học như một lộ trình để đạt được quyền định cư hoặc tiếp cận thị trường lao động nước sở tại. Với R2Q7, quét đoạn 5 tìm từ khóa "Gulf states" để làm rõ phản ứng của họ: thiết lập các cơ sở/chi nhánh của các trường đại học nước ngoài có tiếng ngay trong biên giới quốc gia thay vì gửi sinh viên ra nước ngoài. Với R2Q8, quét đoạn 4 tìm từ khóa liên quan đến mối bận tâm ("concern") của các quốc gia tiếp nhận: họ phải cân nhắc xem hệ thống visa sinh viên có đang hoạt động đúng thiết kế hay thực chất đã biến thành một kênh nhập cư thay thế.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Từ vựng trong ngữ cảnh (R2Q4, R2Q6): Sử dụng kỹ năng phân tích Context Clues (Manh mối ngữ cảnh). Với R2Q4, từ "migration-linked" được văn bản giải thích ngay ở mệnh đề sau dấu gạch ngang hoặc ngữ cảnh kế cận: liên quan đến mục tiêu đạt được quyền thường trú hoặc lao động tại nước đến hơn là thăng tiến học thuật đơn thuần. Với R2Q6, từ "decoupled" nằm trong ngữ cảnh giả định "việc tiếp cận giáo dục chất lượng cao bắt buộc phải dịch chuyển thể chất" không còn hoàn toàn đúng, mang nghĩa là bị tách rời, không còn gắn chặt với nhau, tương đương với "separated".
  • Dạng câu hỏi Loại trừ NOT (R2Q9): Tiến hành đối soát các xu hướng tạo nên cục diện đa cực tại đoạn 5. Bài viết gọi tên sự trỗi dậy của Trung Quốc, Singapore, Malaysia, các chương trình dạy bằng tiếng Anh miễn/giảm học phí của châu Âu và các cơ sở chi nhánh tại vùng Vịnh. Việc giới thiệu các khung bằng cấp quốc tế chuẩn hóa để nhà tuyển dụng công nhận hoàn toàn không được đề cập, nên đây là đáp án cần chọn.

Lời khuyên: Đây là bài đọc thuộc dạng phân tích lịch sử - chính sách với lượng thông tin hàn lâm tương đối dày. Bạn nên làm các câu Từ vựng (R2Q4, R2Q6) trước để khởi động. Tiếp theo, dùng từ khóa quét nhanh thông tin cho các câu Chi tiết (R2Q2, R2Q3, R2Q5, R2Q7, R2Q8) và câu NOT (R2Q9). Cuối cùng, tổng hợp toàn bộ các giai đoạn phát triển của dòng chảy giáo dục để chốt đáp án cho câu Ý chính (R2Q1) và câu Suy luận (R2Q10).

questions.question: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: International education has shifted from an idealist project of cross-cultural exchange to a commercial enterprise driven primarily by the revenue needs of universities in English-speaking countries.

The movement of students across borders has always been shaped by a combination of political, commercial, and individual factors, and understanding it requires recognizing the complexity of all these dimensions together.

The rise of new education hubs in Asia and the Gulf has fundamentally undermined the dominance of Western universities, redistributing global student flows in ways that reflect a broader shift in geopolitical power.

Advances in online learning technology are gradually replacing physical international student mobility, making the traditional model of overseas study increasingly difficult to justify on purely educational grounds.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was the founding purpose of programs like the Fulbright Scholarship established after World War II?
options: To generate revenue for universities in North America and Western Europe at a time when domestic student enrollment was declining due to postwar economic hardship.
To establish a network of academic institutions aligned with Western political values that could counterbalance the influence of Soviet-funded education programs.
To provide students from developing countries with the academic qualifications needed to contribute to national economic development upon returning home.
To reduce international tensions by forming personal and intellectual connections between citizens of different countries through educational exchange.

questions.question: According to the passage, what was one consequence of universities in English-speaking countries actively recruiting fee-paying international students from the 1980s onward?
options: Public funding for higher education in receiving countries increased substantially as governments recognized the economic value of attracting large numbers of overseas students.
International students began choosing destinations based primarily on the strength of scholarship programs rather than on the academic reputation of specific universities.
Universities in non-English-speaking countries began offering more programs taught in English in order to compete with institutions in the United Kingdom, Australia, and Canada.
The growth of a commercial recruitment industry introduced market-driven priorities into admissions decisions that had previously been guided mainly by academic considerations.

questions.question: The word "migration-linked" in paragraph 4 is closest in meaning to _______.
options: associated with the temporary relocation of students who intend to return to their home countries immediately after completing their degrees
connected to the goal of obtaining permanent residency or employment rights in the destination country rather than primarily pursuing academic advancement
tied to government-funded scholarship programs that require recipients to work in a specific sector upon returning to their country of origin
related to the movement of students between multiple countries during a single period of study rather than committing to a single overseas destination

questions.question: According to the passage, what shift occurred in international students' motivations between the early 2000s and the 2010s?
options: Students moved away from selecting destinations based on academic reputation and increasingly chose overseas study as a route to residency or labor market access in the destination country.
Students shifted from favoring traditional academic disciplines toward vocational and professional programs that offered more direct pathways to employment in the destination country.
Students shifted from prioritizing the prestige of individual professors toward seeking programs that offered the strongest alumni networks in their chosen professional fields.
Students began preferring shorter exchange programs over full degree programs abroad, reflecting a desire to gain international experience without committing to a multi-year overseas education.

questions.question: The word "decoupled" in paragraph 6 is closest in meaning to _______.
options: separated
undermined
complicated
reinforced

questions.question: According to the passage, how have Gulf states responded to shifts in the international education landscape?
options: They have sought to establish campuses of well-regarded foreign universities within their own national borders rather than sending students abroad.
They have established their own universities with instruction delivered entirely in Arabic in order to reduce their dependence on foreign academic institutions.
They have offered full scholarships to attract high-achieving international students who would otherwise choose universities in Europe or North America.
They have developed low-cost online education partnerships with prestigious universities to make international qualifications accessible to domestic students.

questions.question: According to the passage, what concern has the rise of migration-linked motivations among international students created for receiving countries?
options: Receiving countries have had to consider whether their student visa systems are operating as designed or have effectively become alternative immigration channels.
Receiving countries have struggled to prevent universities from exploiting migration-linked students by offering low-quality programs that prioritize visa access over genuine academic content.

Receiving countries have become concerned that migration-linked students are less academically prepared than those motivated purely by educational goals, lowering the overall quality of their university programs.
Receiving countries have faced pressure from home governments to limit the number of migration-linked students admitted, in order to preserve bilateral educational exchange agreements.

questions.question: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT mentioned as a development that has contributed to the more multipolar international education landscape described in paragraph 5?
options: European countries offering English-taught programs with low or no tuition fees as part of deliberate strategies to attract international students.
The emergence of China, Singapore, and Malaysia as regional education centers attracting students who previously would have traveled to Western destinations.
Gulf states hosting branch campuses of prestigious foreign universities on their own territory as a way of building local educational capacity.
The introduction of standardized international qualification frameworks that have made degrees from non-Western universities more widely recognized by employers.

questions.question: What can be inferred about the author's view of online learning as a replacement for physical international student mobility?
options: The author believes online learning will eventually render physical student mobility unnecessary, as improvements in virtual platforms make it increasingly possible to replicate the full overseas study experience.

The author suggests that while online learning has expanded access for students who cannot afford overseas study, it has not replaced physical mobility because the social and professional dimensions of studying abroad remain hard to reproduce virtually.

The author implies that online learning has already disrupted international student mobility more substantially than official enrollment figures suggest, since many students now combine short physical stays with longer periods of remote study.

The author argues that online learning primarily benefits institutions in wealthy countries, which can now recruit fee-paying students from lower-income countries without providing them with the full experience of overseas study.

passage.title: The Socio-Economic Legacy of the COVID-19 Pandemic
passage.text:
When the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a global pandemic in March 2020, governments and economists alike scrambled to anticipate the scale of disruption that lay ahead. Few, however, predicted with accuracy the particular shape that disruption would take — not a uniform global recession followed by uniform recovery, but a deeply uneven fracturing of economies, labor markets, and social systems that exposed and amplified pre-existing inequalities in ways that will reverberate for decades. [1] The pandemic did not create the vulnerabilities it laid bare; it found them already embedded in the structures of contemporary societies and subjected them to a stress test of unprecedented severity.

Among the most immediate and visible economic consequences was the catastrophic disruption to global supply chains. The simultaneous closure of factories, ports, and logistics networks across multiple continents produced shortages of goods ranging from semiconductors and pharmaceuticals to basic consumer products, revealing the degree to which the efficiency-driven model of globalized production had traded resilience for cost minimization. Companies that had adopted just-in-time inventory systems — holding minimal stock in order to reduce warehousing costs — found themselves unable to meet demand surges that emerged as lockdowns lifted in different regions at different times. The resulting inflationary pressures, which persisted well beyond the acute phase of the pandemic, contributed to a cost-of-living crisis whose effects were felt most acutely by households with the least capacity to absorb rising prices.

The labor market consequences of the pandemic were no less profound, and considerably more complex than early analyses suggested. The initial wave of job losses was concentrated in sectors requiring physical presence — hospitality, retail, transportation, and personal services — which disproportionately employed lower-wage workers, women, and younger people. As governments in wealthier countries deployed large-scale income support measures, including furlough schemes and direct cash transfers, the worst predictions of mass unemployment were averted in the short term. Yet these interventions masked significant structural changes that became apparent only as support programs were withdrawn. Labor force participation rates in many countries failed to return to pre-pandemic levels, as a substantial cohort of older workers opted for early retirement and many parents — again, disproportionately women — found that the collapse of childcare infrastructure made sustained employment unmanageable.

Perhaps the most consequential and lasting transformation catalyzed by the pandemic was the accelerated normalization of remote work across a broad range of professional occupations. Prior to 2020, remote work existed as a marginal practice available to a small minority of knowledge workers; within months of the first lockdowns, it had become the operational default for hundreds of millions of people globally. Research conducted in the aftermath of these shifts found that worker preferences had been durably altered: large proportions of those who had experienced remote work expressed reluctance to return to full-time office arrangements, and many indicated that flexibility of location had become a primary consideration in employment decisions. Employers responded with varying degrees of accommodation, and the resulting negotiations over hybrid arrangements became one of the defining workplace dynamics of the mid-2020s. The broader spatial consequences of this shift — including the partial hollowing out of central business districts, the redistribution of residential demand toward suburban and rural areas, and the emergence of new patterns of urban inequality — have yet to fully resolve.

The pandemic's impact on educational systems constitutes another dimension of its socio-economic legacy that merits particular attention. School closures of varying duration affected children in nearly every country, with UNESCO estimating that at the peak of disruption, over 1.5 billion learners were kept out of classrooms. The shift to remote learning exposed stark disparities in access to digital infrastructure, with students in lower-income households and less well-resourced school systems facing far greater obstacles to continued education than their more affluent peers. [2] Research published in subsequent years documented measurable learning losses across cohorts affected by extended school closures, with evidence suggesting that the losses were greatest among students from disadvantaged backgrounds — compounding existing achievement gaps rather than creating new ones. The long-term labor market implications of these learning losses, particularly for cohorts who were at critical developmental stages during the disruption, remain a subject of active concern among economists and education researchers.

The fiscal response to the pandemic was extraordinary in both scale and speed. Governments collectively injected trillions of dollars into their economies through a combination of direct expenditure, loan guarantees, and monetary policy interventions, driving public debt levels in many countries to heights not seen since the aftermath of World War II. The long-term sustainability of these debt levels, and the distributional consequences of the fiscal consolidation measures that governments have subsequently pursued, have become central fault lines in post-pandemic economic policy debates. [3] Critics have argued that austerity measures adopted in the wake of pandemic spending have fallen disproportionately on public services already under strain, while proponents have maintained that debt stabilization is a prerequisite for the long-term investment in infrastructure and human capital that a genuine post-pandemic recovery requires.

What distinguishes the socio-economic legacy of COVID-19 from that of earlier crises is not simply its scale but the particular way in which it interacted with existing trajectories of change. Many of the transformations it accelerated — the digitization of work, the fragility of global supply chains, the inadequacy of social protection systems for non-standard workers — were already underway before March 2020. [4] The pandemic compressed what might otherwise have been a decade of gradual transition into two years of forced adaptation, leaving institutions, labor markets, and individuals with insufficient time to adjust. Whether the legacy of that compression proves ultimately to be a durable acceleration of necessary modernization or a set of unresolved disruptions that will constrain economic and social development for a generation remains one of the defining open questions of the contemporary era.

tasks.suggestion:
Để đạt kết quả tốt cho phần thi này, bạn nên áp dụng các chiến thuật sau đây:

  • Dạng câu hỏi Ý chính (R3Q1): Sử dụng kỹ năng Skimming (Đọc lướt). Tập trung đọc kỹ đoạn 1 và đoạn cuối để nhận diện mạch lập luận. Bài viết không chỉ xoay quanh chuỗi cung ứng hay làm việc từ xa. Luận điểm bao quát là di sản kinh tế - xã hội của COVID-19 mang tính bất bình đẳng sâu sắc, làm gia tăng và trầm trọng hóa những bất ổn vốn có trong thị trường lao động, hệ thống giáo dục và tài chính công.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Chi tiết (R3Q2, R3Q4, R3Q5, R3Q6, R3Q8): Sử dụng kỹ năng Scanning (Đọc quét) để định vị thông tin dựa trên từ khóa. Với R3Q2, quét đoạn 2 tìm từ khóa "just-in-time" để thấy lỗ hổng: mô hình sản xuất toàn cầu ưu tiên tối ưu hóa chi phí hơn là khả năng phục hồi, khiến các doanh nghiệp không kịp trở tay trước sự bùng nổ nhu cầu đột biến khi gỡ bỏ phong tỏa. Với R3Q4, quét đoạn 3 về thị trường lao động để xác định đối tượng chịu tổn thất lớn nhất: người lao động ở các ngành yêu cầu sự hiện diện thể chất (dịch vụ, bán lẻ, khách sạn), lao động thu nhập thấp, phụ nữ và giới trẻ. Với R3Q5, quét đoạn 4 về làm việc từ xa để thấy sự thay đổi lâu dài: phần lớn người lao động không muốn quay lại văn phòng toàn thời gian và bắt đầu coi sự linh hoạt về vị trí là yếu tố tiên quyết khi chọn việc. Với R3Q6, quét đoạn 5 tìm từ khóa "school closures" hoặc "learning losses" để thấy kết luận của nghiên cứu: tổn thất học tập nghiêm trọng nhất ở học sinh thuộc nhóm yếu thế, làm nới rộng khoảng cách thành tích đã tồn tại từ trước. Với R3Q8, quét đoạn 6 về chính sách tài khóa để làm rõ mâu thuẫn: phía chỉ trích cho rằng thắt chặt tài khóa làm kiệt quệ các dịch vụ công vốn đã căng thẳng, trong khi phía ủng hộ lập luận rằng ổn định nợ là điều kiện bắt buộc để đầu tư phục hồi dài hạn.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Quy chiếu (R3Q3): Tìm đại từ "themselves" ở đoạn 2. Đọc ngược lại cấu trúc câu phức để xác định chủ thể thực hiện hành động "unable to meet demand surges" (không thể đáp ứng nhu cầu tăng vọt). Chủ thể đó chính là các công ty đã áp dụng hệ thống kiểm kho just-in-time.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Loại trừ NOT (R3Q7): Đối soát các hệ quả không gian của làm việc từ xa tại đoạn 4. Văn bản liệt kê: sự sụt giảm hoạt động ở khu trung tâm, nhu cầu nhà ở dịch chuyển ra ngoại ô/nông thôn, và mô hình bất bình đẳng đô thị mới. Xu hướng giảm di cư quốc tế đến các thành phố lớn không được đề cập, nên đây là đáp án đúng.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Suy luận & Chèn câu (R3Q9, R3Q10): Với R3Q9, đọc kỹ đoạn cuối để suy luận: việc nén một thập kỷ thay đổi vào hai năm dịch bệnh đã khiến các thể chế và cá nhân không có đủ thời gian thích nghi, để lại những câu hỏi chưa có lời giải về việc liệu sự đứt gãy này là tiến bộ hay tổn hại lâu dài. Với R3Q10, câu cần chèn làm rõ rằng "những sự chênh lệch này khớp chính xác với mô hình phân tầng kinh tế - xã hội có từ nhiều năm trước". Vị trí [2] là vị trí hoàn hảo nhất vì nó đứng ngay sau câu mô tả sự phân hóa giàu nghèo, tổn thương của các nhóm yếu thế trong đại dịch, giúp củng cố và giải thích cho luận điểm bất bình đẳng đó.

Lời khuyên: Đây là bài đọc có cấu trúc phân tích nghị luận xã hội - kinh tế rất mạch lạc. Hãy xử lý câu hỏi Quy chiếu (R3Q3) đầu tiên để khởi động nhanh. Tiếp theo, bám sát các từ khóa rõ ràng để giải quyết các câu Chi tiết (R3Q2, R3Q4, R3Q5, R3Q6, R3Q8) và câu NOT (R3Q7). Hãy để các câu đòi hỏi tư duy tổng hợp cao như câu Ý chính (R3Q1), câu Suy luận (R3Q9) và Chèn câu (R3Q10) làm ở lượt cuối cùng để đảm bảo tính chính xác tuyệt đối.

questions.question: What is the central argument of the passage?
options: The most consequential outcome of the pandemic was the permanent normalization of remote work, which has reshaped urban economies and labor markets more fundamentally than any other aspect of the crisis.

The socio-economic legacy of COVID-19 is characterized by deep unevenness, accelerating and amplifying pre-existing inequalities across labor markets, education systems, and public finances in ways that remain unresolved.
The COVID-19 pandemic caused unprecedented economic damage primarily through its disruption of global supply chains, which proved far more fragile than economists had previously recognized.

Governments' fiscal responses to the pandemic, while effective in preventing mass unemployment in the short term, have created a long-term debt burden that will require generations of austerity to address.

questions.question: According to the passage, what specific vulnerability in the global production model did the pandemic's supply chain disruptions reveal?
options: The absence of international agreements requiring countries to maintain minimum reserves of essential goods such as pharmaceuticals and semiconductors.
The prioritization of cost efficiency over resilience in supply chain design, with just-in-time inventory systems leaving companies unable to meet uneven demand surges.
The excessive dependence of global manufacturing on a small number of countries that were unwilling to continue exporting during a health emergency.
The failure of multinational corporations to invest in domestic production capacity, leaving entire sectors dependent on overseas suppliers during a period of closed borders.

questions.question: The word "themselves" in paragraph 2 refers to _______.
options: the economists and government officials who had failed to predict the particular form that pandemic-related economic disruption would take
the lower-income households that were most severely affected by the inflationary pressures that followed supply chain disruptions
the companies that had adopted just-in-time inventory systems and consequently could not satisfy demand when lockdowns began lifting
the factories, ports, and logistics networks that were simultaneously closed across multiple continents during the early phase of the pandemic

questions.question: According to the passage, which groups were most disproportionately affected by the initial wave of pandemic-related job losses?
options: Older workers approaching retirement age, who were encouraged by employers to take early exit packages in order to reduce payroll costs during a period of collapsing revenue.
Employees in sectors requiring physical presence, including lower-wage workers, women, and younger people employed in hospitality, retail, and personal services.
Workers in manufacturing and logistics sectors, whose jobs were eliminated when factories and distribution centers closed as part of government-mandated lockdown measures.
Knowledge workers and senior professionals, whose complex roles could not easily be transferred to remote settings during the rapid transition to home-based work.

questions.question: According to the passage, how did the pandemic durably alter worker preferences regarding remote work arrangements?
options: Workers who had practiced remote work during lockdowns acquired new digital skills that made them more competitive in the labor market and less dependent on specific employers or office locations.
Workers developed a preference for fully remote rather than hybrid arrangements, causing significant conflict with employers who insisted that some degree of in-person collaboration was essential.

Large proportions of workers who had experienced remote work were reluctant to return to full-time office settings and began treating locational flexibility as a primary factor in employment decisions.
Workers who experienced remote work became significantly more productive and reported higher job satisfaction, leading them to resist any return to office-based employment.

questions.question: According to the passage, which finding regarding pandemic-related learning losses is specifically supported by research conducted after school closures ended?
options: Students who attended well-resourced schools recovered their learning losses within two years, while students from disadvantaged backgrounds continued to fall behind at an accelerating rate.
The learning losses documented across all cohorts were smaller than initially predicted, suggesting that remote learning was more effective than early assessments of its quality had indicated.
Students at critical developmental stages during the pandemic showed the greatest resilience, recovering learning losses more quickly than older students who had more established academic habits.
The learning losses caused by school closures were greatest among students from disadvantaged backgrounds, widening achievement gaps that had already existed before the pandemic.

questions.question: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT mentioned as a spatial consequence of the widespread shift to remote work?
options: A partial decline in economic activity in central business districts as fewer workers commuted to city centers on a daily basis.
A decline in international migration to major cities, as remote work eliminated the professional incentive for workers in other countries to relocate to urban employment hubs.
An increase in residential demand in suburban and rural areas as workers relocated away from urban centers where office proximity had previously been necessary.
The emergence of new patterns of urban inequality as the spatial redistribution of economic activity produced uneven outcomes across different neighborhoods and communities.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the central disagreement between critics and proponents of post-pandemic fiscal consolidation measures?
options: Critics argue that governments borrowed excessively during the pandemic and should have relied more heavily on monetary policy, while proponents maintain that direct expenditure was the only tool capable of preventing economic collapse.

Critics believe that debt levels accumulated during the pandemic are unsustainable and require immediate large-scale reduction, while proponents argue that gradual debt reduction over several decades is both economically sufficient and politically feasible.

Critics maintain that emergency fiscal measures should have been targeted more narrowly at the most affected sectors, while proponents argue that broad-based support was essential to prevent social instability during the acute phase of the crisis.

Critics contend that fiscal consolidation has disproportionately burdened already strained public services, while proponents argue that stabilizing debt is a necessary condition for the long-term investment a genuine recovery requires.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the final paragraph about the relationship between the pandemic's pace of change and the capacity of institutions to adapt?
options: Institutions that had already begun modernizing before 2020 were able to absorb the pandemic's disruptions with minimal lasting damage, while those that had resisted change suffered disproportionately.

The pace of pandemic-driven transformation has made it impossible for governments to develop coherent long-term economic strategies, condemning post-pandemic policy to reactive short-termism for the foreseeable future.

The pandemic demonstrated that most institutions are fundamentally more adaptable than pre-crisis analyses had suggested, with the speed of adjustment to remote work and digital services exceeding even optimistic forecasts.

The compression of a decade's worth of change into two years left institutions, labor markets, and individuals with insufficient time to adapt, raising unresolved questions about whether the resulting disruptions represent progress or lasting harm.

passage.title: The Psychology and Physics of Color Perception
passage.text:
Color is among the most immediate and seemingly self-evident features of visual experience, yet it is also among the most philosophically and scientifically vexing. What we ordinarily call the color of an object is neither a simple physical property of that object nor a straightforward neural response to electromagnetic radiation, but rather an emergent product of the interaction between physical wavelengths, the biological architecture of the visual system, and the interpretive processes of the brain — processes so rapid, so automatic, and so deeply conditioned by prior experience that their constructed character is almost entirely invisible to introspection. [1] Understanding color perception requires traversing several disciplines simultaneously: the physics of light, the physiology of the retina, the neuroscience of visual processing, and the psychology of perceptual inference — none of which, in isolation, is sufficient to account for the full richness of chromatic experience.

The physical substrate of color is electromagnetic radiation within the visible spectrum, conventionally defined as wavelengths ranging from approximately 380 nanometres at the violet end to approximately 700 nanometres at the red end. Objects do not possess color in the way they possess mass or electrical charge; rather, they selectively absorb and reflect different wavelengths depending on the molecular structure of their surfaces. A ripe tomato appears red not because it inherently contains redness but because the pigments in its skin absorb most wavelengths of incident light while reflecting those in the longer-wavelength range that the human visual system interprets as red. This selective reflectance is a stable physical property of the object's surface, but the color experienced by an observer is not: it depends critically on the spectral composition of the illuminant, the reflectance properties of surrounding objects, and the prior adaptation state of the observer's visual system — all factors that vary continuously and independently of the object itself.

The biological transduction of wavelength information into color experience begins in the retina, where three distinct populations of cone photoreceptors — designated S, M, and L for their sensitivity peaks in the short, medium, and long wavelength ranges — respond differentially to incoming light. The critical insight that emerges from the trichromatic architecture of human color vision is that the visual system does not encode wavelength directly; it encodes the ratios of activation across the three cone types, a scheme that has both remarkable advantages and "fundamental limitations." The advantage is parsimony: an enormous range of spectral stimuli can be represented through just three channels. The limitation is metameric equivalence: two physically distinct spectral distributions can produce identical cone activation ratios and are therefore perceptually indistinguishable, a phenomenon known as metamerism that has significant practical implications for color reproduction in printing, photography, and display technology.

The output of the retinal cone system is not transmitted directly to higher cortical areas as a trichromatic signal; it undergoes a fundamental recoding in the retinal ganglion cells and lateral geniculate nucleus into an opponent color system. In this scheme, the brain does not represent color as three independent channels but as three opponent pairs: light versus dark, red versus green, and blue versus yellow. This opponent organization, first proposed by the physiologist Ewald Hering in the nineteenth century and later confirmed by electrophysiological recording, accounts for a range of phenomena that trichromatic theory alone cannot explain — including the impossibility of perceiving certain color combinations (there is no perceptual experience of "reddish-green" or "yellowish-blue"), the structure of simultaneous color contrast effects, and the pattern of color afterimages produced by prolonged fixation on a chromatic stimulus. [2]

Beyond the retina and early visual pathway, color processing involves a distributed network of cortical areas whose functional contributions are only partially understood. Area V4 in the ventral visual stream has long been associated with color constancy — the remarkable ability of the visual system to maintain a stable perception of an object's color despite dramatic changes in illumination. A tomato appears red whether viewed in the yellow light of an incandescent bulb, the bluish light of an overcast sky, or the greenish light filtering through a forest canopy, even though the actual wavelengths reflected from its surface differ substantially across these conditions. Computational models of color constancy suggest that the visual system achieves this feat by "discounting" the illuminant — inferring the spectral properties of the light source from contextual information in the scene and adjusting its color estimates accordingly. The neural mechanisms through which this inferential process is implemented remain an active area of investigation. [3]

The psychological dimensions of color perception extend well beyond the neural processing of wavelength information to encompass learned associations, cultural conventions, and the complex interactions between color and other perceptual and cognitive systems. Research in cross-cultural psychology has documented substantial variation in the way different linguistic communities categorize and name colors, with some languages drawing boundaries between color categories at points where others see a single continuous region of the spectrum. The influential Sapir-Whorf hypothesis, in its strong form, predicted that such linguistic differences would produce corresponding perceptual differences — that speakers of languages with different color lexicons would literally see the world differently. Subsequent experimental evidence has produced a more nuanced picture: linguistic categories appear to influence color discrimination most strongly in tasks that engage verbal or categorical processing, while their effects on low-level perceptual sensitivity are considerably more modest. [4]

The interaction between color and the other senses further complicates any simple account of color as a visual phenomenon. Crossmodal associations between color and sound, taste, smell, and touch — studied under the framework of synesthesia and its weaker analogs in the general population — reveal that color experience is not confined to the visual system but is deeply integrated with multimodal cognitive representations. Foods presented in incongruent colors are consistently rated as less flavorful, wines described with color-biased vocabulary show measurable effects on tasters' reported flavor profiles, and environments decorated in particular hues reliably influence occupants' thermal comfort ratings and pain tolerance thresholds. These findings suggest that what we experience as the simple, direct perception of color is in fact the output of a deeply integrative cognitive process — one in which the nominally visual quality of hue is inseparable from the broader network of meaning, memory, and embodied experience within which it is embedded.

The question of whether color, understood in this full sense, is in the object, in the observer, or in the relationship between them does not admit of a simple answer — and the scientific literature has not converged on one. What the accumulated evidence does suggest is that color perception is neither the passive registration of a physical property nor the unconstrained projection of a mental image, but a sophisticated inferential achievement that the brain accomplishes so fluently, and under such a wide range of conditions, that its complexity remains permanently concealed behind the apparent simplicity of seeing a red tomato on a white table.

tasks.suggestion:
Để đạt kết quả tốt cho phần thi này, bạn nên áp dụng các chiến thuật sau đây:

  • Dạng câu hỏi Ý chính & Chiến lược tiếp cận toàn cục (R4Q1, R4Q9): Sử dụng kỹ năng Skimming (Đọc lướt). Đọc kỹ đoạn đầu và đoạn kết để nắm bắt ý đồ hệ thống của tác giả. Bài đọc đưa ra một góc nhìn đa ngành về bản chất của màu sắc. Với R4Q1, đáp án chính xác phải phản ánh đầy đủ tính chất tích hợp này: màu sắc không phải là một đặc tính cố định của vật thể hay của người quan sát, mà là một sản phẩm phái sinh ("emergent product") đan xen từ các quá trình vật lý, sinh học, thần kinh học và tâm lý học. Với R4Q9, thái độ của tác giả là một sự cân bằng phân tích ("analytically balanced"), nhìn nhận cơ chế tri giác màu sắc là một hiện tượng vô cùng phức tạp, đòi hỏi sự giao thoa của nhiều ngành khoa học để lý giải và nhiều câu hỏi cốt lõi vẫn đang bỏ ngỏ.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Chi tiết (R4Q2, R4Q4, R4Q6, R4Q8): Sử dụng kỹ năng Scanning (Đọc quét) để dò tìm từ khóa chính xác trong văn bản gốc. Với R4Q2, quét đoạn 2 để thấy lý do màu sắc không đại diện cho đặc tính vật lý ổn định: trải nghiệm màu sắc phụ thuộc chặt chẽ vào thành phần phổ của nguồn sáng, sự phản xạ của các vật thể xung quanh và trạng thái thích ứng của người quan sát. Với R4Q4, quét đoạn 4 tìm từ khóa "opponent color system" để thấy hiện tượng mà lý thuyết tam sắc không giải thích được: sự bất khả thi khi trải nghiệm các tổ hợp màu đối nghịch như xanh lá - đỏ hoặc vàng - xanh dương. Với R4Q6, quét đoạn 5 về cơ chế hằng định màu sắc ("color constancy"): hệ thống thị giác đạt được điều này bằng cách suy diễn các đặc tính phổ của nguồn sáng từ thông tin bối cảnh của cảnh vật, từ đó điều chỉnh các ước tính màu sắc để bù đắp cho ảnh hưởng của nguồn sáng. Với R4Q8, quét đoạn 6 tìm từ khóa "Sapir-Whorf hypothesis" để làm rõ mối quan hệ giữa ngôn ngữ và tri giác: các bằng chứng thực nghiệm ủng hộ một phiên bản có giới hạn, theo đó các phạm trù ngôn ngữ ảnh hưởng mạnh nhất đến các tác vụ phân biệt màu sắc có liên quan đến xử lý ngôn từ, trong khi tác động của chúng lên độ nhạy tri giác bậc thấp là yếu hơn đáng kể.
  • Dạng câu hỏi Từ vựng trong ngữ cảnh (R4Q3, R4Q5): Sử dụng phân tích Context Clues để giải mã thuật ngữ chuyên ngành. Với R4Q3, cụm từ "fundamental limitations" nói về giới hạn của cơ chế mã hóa tam sắc, được giải thích ngay sau đó bằng hiện tượng metamerism — thực tế là hai phổ ánh sáng vật lý khác nhau hoàn toàn có thể tạo ra các mô hình kích hoạt tế bào nón y hệt nhau, khiến chúng không thể phân biệt được về mặt tri giác. Với R4Q5, từ "discounting" đặt trong ngữ cảnh bộ não xử lý và loại trừ tầm ảnh hưởng của nguồn sáng chiếu tớ để giữ màu sắc vật thể ổn định, do đó nó đồng nghĩa với cụm "neutralizing the influence of".
  • Dạng câu hỏi Quy chiếu (R4Q7): Tìm đại từ "they" ở đoạn 2. Đọc ngược lại cấu trúc câu: "Objects do not possess color in the way they possess mass or electrical charge". Cấu trúc so sánh song song chỉ ra "they" ở đây quy chiếu trực tiếp đến các vật thể ("objects").
  • Dạng câu hỏi Loại trừ NOT (R4Q10): Tiến hành đối soát các ví dụ về tác động phi thị giác của màu sắc ở đoạn 7. Văn bản có nhắc đến thực phẩm sai màu ăn bớt ngon, từ ngữ tả rượu vang định hình hương vị cảm nhận, và màu sắc môi trường ảnh hưởng đến cảm giác nhiệt độ và ngưỡng chịu đau. Việc đọc văn bản mực đỏ làm suy giảm khả năng củng cố trí nhớ hoàn toàn không xuất hiện, do đó đây là đáp án cần chọn.

Lời khuyên: Đối với một bài đọc phân tầng học thuật cao như Part 4 này, hãy ưu tiên giải quyết nhanh câu Quy chiếu (R4Q7) và câu Từ vựng (R4Q3, R4Q5) trước. Tiếp theo, bám chắc từ khóa để định vị các câu hỏi Chi tiết (R4Q2, R4Q4, R4Q6, R4Q8) và câu hỏi NOT (R4Q10). Chỉ khi đã hoàn thành các câu hỏi định vị này và nắm được bộ khung lập luận của tác giả, bạn mới nên chốt câu Ý chính (R4Q1) và câu Thái độ (R4Q9) để đạt độ chính xác cao nhất.

questions.question: What is the central claim of the passage?
options: The most important unresolved question in color science is whether linguistic categories genuinely alter low-level perceptual sensitivity, a question that current experimental methods are not yet sophisticated enough to answer definitively.

Color is not a fixed property of either objects or observers but an emergent product of physical, biological, neurological, and psychological processes whose full complexity is concealed by the apparent immediacy of visual experience.

Color perception is primarily a physiological phenomenon whose complexity stems from the trichromatic architecture of cone photoreceptors rather than from higher cortical processing or cultural conditioning.

Advances in understanding the opponent color system and cortical color constancy mechanisms have largely resolved the classical debate between trichromatic and opponent-process theories of color vision.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is the color perceived by an observer not a reliable indicator of a stable physical property of the object being viewed?
options: The three cone populations in the human retina respond to overlapping wavelength ranges, making it impossible for the visual system to extract precise wavelength information from any single object.

The color experience depends on the spectral composition of the light source, the reflectance of surrounding objects, and the observer's adaptation state — all of which vary independently of the object itself.

Objects alter their selective reflectance properties over time in response to environmental factors such as temperature and humidity, meaning that the same object reflects different wavelengths under different storage conditions.

The opponent color system in the visual cortex actively suppresses certain wavelength combinations, meaning that the brain never receives a complete representation of the full spectral reflectance of any viewed object.

questions.question: The phrase "fundamental limitations" in paragraph 3 refers to which constraint of the trichromatic encoding scheme?
options: The inability of the cone system to detect wavelengths beyond the conventional visible spectrum, leaving the visual system blind to ultraviolet and infrared radiation that other species can perceive.
The fact that two physically different light spectra can produce identical cone activation patterns, making them perceptually indistinguishable despite their objective differences.
The tendency of the three cone types to become progressively less sensitive with age, producing a gradual narrowing of the range of colors that older observers can reliably distinguish.
The dependence of cone sensitivity peaks on prior light exposure, meaning that the visual system's color encoding shifts unpredictably depending on the adaptation history of each individual observer.

questions.question: According to the passage, which specific perceptual phenomenon does the opponent color system account for that trichromatic theory alone cannot explain?
options: The progressive deterioration of color discrimination in peripheral vision, where cone density is lower and the visual system relies more heavily on rod photoreceptors sensitive only to luminance.

The impossibility of experiencing certain color combinations, such as reddish-green or yellowish-blue, which do not exist as perceptual experiences despite the physical existence of their component wavelengths.
The ability of the visual system to perceive a continuous gradient of color across the full visible spectrum rather than experiencing discrete jumps between individual wavelength categories.
The fact that two physically distinct light spectra can produce the same color experience when they generate equivalent patterns of cone activation across the three photoreceptor populations.

questions.question: The word "discounting" in paragraph 5 is closest in meaning to _______.
options: statistically averaging
selectively suppressing
neutralizing the influence of
amplifying

questions.question: According to the passage, how does the visual system achieve color constancy despite changes in illumination?
options: It infers the spectral characteristics of the light source from contextual scene information and adjusts its color estimates to compensate for the illuminant's influence on the wavelengths reaching the eye.

It averages the wavelength information received across a large visual field, using the statistical properties of natural scenes to generate a stable estimate of each object's true surface reflectance.

It compares the wavelengths reflected from a target object against a stored memory representation of that object's canonical color, using the discrepancy to calculate a corrective adjustment to the perceived hue.

It relies on specialized cells in area V4 that respond only to the longest wavelengths reflected from an object's surface, providing a stable signal that is unaffected by changes in the spectral composition of ambient light.

questions.question: The word "they" in paragraph 2 refers to _______.
options: objects, which do not inherently contain the colors they appear to have but instead selectively reflect certain wavelengths depending on their surface properties
the pigments present in the surface of a ripe tomato that absorb most incoming wavelengths while reflecting those in the longer-wavelength range
the wavelengths of electromagnetic radiation within the visible spectrum that are selectively absorbed or reflected by the molecular structure of object surfaces
observers, whose prior adaptation state and visual system architecture determine the color experience produced by any given pattern of wavelength reflectance

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the experimental evidence regarding the Sapir-Whorf hypothesis suggest about the relationship between language and color perception?
options: The evidence fully confirms the strong version of the hypothesis, demonstrating that speakers of languages with different color lexicons experience measurably different perceptual sensitivities to wavelengths near the boundaries of their linguistic color categories.

The evidence refutes the hypothesis entirely, showing that color perception is determined exclusively by the biological architecture of the visual system and is unaffected by the linguistic categories available to the observer.

The evidence supports a qualified version in which linguistic categories influence color discrimination most strongly in tasks involving verbal processing, while their effects on low-level perceptual sensitivity are considerably weaker.

The evidence suggests that the hypothesis applies only to observers who are simultaneously fluent in two languages with different color lexicons, as bilingual individuals show the strongest effects of linguistic framing on color discrimination tasks.

questions.question: Which of the following best characterizes the author's overall stance toward the scientific understanding of color perception?
options: The author is optimistic that emerging neuroscientific techniques will soon resolve the remaining uncertainties about color perception, particularly regarding the cortical mechanisms underlying color constancy and crossmodal color associations.

The author is implicitly critical of psychological and cultural approaches to color, suggesting that the physics and physiology of color vision provide the only scientifically rigorous framework for understanding chromatic experience.

The author is cautiously skeptical of computational models of color constancy, implying that their explanatory success in controlled laboratory settings does not necessarily reflect the actual mechanisms operating in the living visual system.

The author maintains an analytically balanced position, presenting color perception as a genuinely complex phenomenon whose full explanation requires multiple disciplines and whose deepest questions remain open.

questions.question: According to the passage, which of the following is NOT mentioned as an example of color influencing a non-visual perceptual or cognitive outcome?
options: Foods displayed in colors that do not match expectations are judged to taste less appealing than the same foods presented in their conventional colors.
The color-inflected vocabulary used to describe wine has a measurable effect on the flavor profiles that tasters subsequently report experiencing.
People exposed to specific environmental colors show reliable differences in their reported comfort with ambient temperature and their tolerance of pain.
Individuals who view written text presented in red ink demonstrate significantly impaired memory consolidation compared to those who read the same text in neutral colors.
